channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Brussels Airlines launches new flights to meet demand for Arctic holidays
item.description: Brussels Airlines said winter trips to the polar region are becoming increasingly popular.

item.title: Flemish community publishes guide to Dutch-speaking schools in Brussels
item.description: The guide brings together contact details and practical information for all Dutch-language schools in Brussels, from nursery to secondary education.

item.title: Eurostar struggles with overcrowding as London terminal remains unchanged
item.description: Some 45,000 passengers pass through Eurostar's cramped London terminal every day, with numbers expected to rise in the coming years. How will the station accommodate them all?

item.title: Can Europe ever be postcolonial? A Brussels museum confronts the afterlife of empire
item.description: At the House of European History, the question mark in the title of its new temporary exhibition, Postcolonial?, does most of the intellectual work.

item.title: Is a shop-free Sunday good for our health?
item.description: From experience, I can say that a country does not necessarily become more vibrant, or people's lives better, just because everything is conveniently available seven days a week.

item.title: Take a break: Best new cafés to try in Brussels
item.description: Whether you're on the hunt for a new spot to take your laptop, some delicious speciality coffee, or somewhere for Sunday brunch, we've got you covered.

item.title: Brussels Airport begins works on new facility to reduce noise pollution for residents
item.description: The enclosure is expected to reduce noise by up to 10 decibels, which means the sound is perceived as roughly half as loud.

item.title: Sainctelette Bridge development takes shape in Brussels
item.description: Traffic on Sainctelette Square is restricted to a single lane as the Molenbeek bridge takes a major step in its renovation.

item.title: New nightclub to open in former bank building in central Brussels
item.description: The club is also set to become a place where Brussels-based artists can bring their own projects to life within the organisation’s studio programme.

item.title: Firefighter killed in gas explosions near Brussels Central, three others injured
item.description: One firefighter was killed. Three people were also seriously injured in the explosions: two Sibelga employees and a second firefighter.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 14 - 16 August
item.description: From the annual dance festival to a world-famous flower display, here's what's on in Brussels this weekend.

item.title: Police seek woman last seen leaving her house in central Brussels
item.description: Police are asking for the public's help to find a 60-year-old woman who has been missing from central Brussels since Wednesday.

item.title: Fire breaks out in restaurant ventilation system in Saint-Gilles
item.description: Firefighters managed to stop a restaurant fire from spreading to apartments above, after a difficult operation in Brussels on Thursday evening.

item.title: Brussels Airport records busiest month since 2019
item.description: Brussels Airport welcomed around 2.6 million passengers in July, making it the airport's busiest month since 2019.

item.title: Why SNCB is cancelling several trains this Friday
item.description: Extreme heat is already disrupting Belgium's railways, with several rush-hour trains cancelled on Friday.

item.title: More Belgians complain about overpriced and botched repairs
item.description: Complaints about overpriced and poorly carried out repairs are mounting in Belgium, prompting a fresh warning to consumers.

item.title: Sweltering heat to start the weekend
item.description: Conditions will become more unsettled on Saturday, although it will remain hot.

item.title: Cycling is booming in Brussels: What should cyclists watch out for?
item.description: With its hilly streets, heavy traffic and once-scarce cycle lanes, Brussels has not always been an obvious city for cyclists. But that is changing fast.

item.title: Brussels' world-famous flower carpet returns to Grand Place on 13 August
item.description: One of the highlights of the cultural calendar is returning to the Belgian capital today – and it is not one to be missed.

item.title: In pictures: How you saw the solar eclipse
item.description: Thousands of people across Belgium went outside to witness the solar eclipse on Wednesday evening. This is what they saw.
